- If sentiment turns sharply bullish (≥1.0) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to over-forecast and overshoots by 1–2% in the next 5–7 days; reduce forecast peak by 1–2%.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) in the last 3–5 days, model under-forecasts; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion.
- When sentiment change is negative and news volume is low (≤2.0), model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect delayed reaction.
- If model forecast peaks > 10% above recent 7-day average, it’s likely over-optimistic; cap forecast at 10% above average or use sentiment decay to smooth.
- If sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) for 5+ days, model tends to drift toward mean; apply slight downward bias (0.5–1.0%) to avoid over-extended rallies.
- If sentiment spikes and news volume is high (≥3.0), model often overreacts; apply 1–2% downward correction to prevent overshoot.
- If true outcome is consistently 0.5–1.5% below model in 3–5 day window, model is biased high; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 30d horizon.
- If sentiment is rising but news volume is low, model may under-react; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to capture sentiment lag.
